cards.summary: An SLO sets a target for an indicator

prompt.text: What is a service level objective?

answer.text: A target for a service level indicator.

options: A target for a service level indicator
correct: A target for a service level indicator

hints: Indicator measures; objective sets the target.

teaching.text: An SLI is the measurement, such as successful requests divided by total requests. An SLO is the target for that measurement, such as 99.9% over 30 days.

teaching.search: SLO vs SLI vs SLA vs Error Budget Google SRE
teaching.alt: A plain-English explanation of SLI, SLO, SLA and the error budget

cards.summary: The error budget is what may fail

prompt.text: If an SLO allows 99.9% success, the remaining 0.1% is the error

answer.text: If an SLO allows 99.9% success, the remaining 0.1% is the error budget.

hints: It is a spending allowance for failure.
cards.fullLine: If an SLO allows 99.9% success, the remaining 0.1% is the error budget.

teaching.text: The error budget turns reliability into a shared number. While budget remains, teams may ship faster. When it is spent, feature work pauses until reliability recovers.

teaching.alt: A monthly reliability target with a small error budget shown as a spending allowance

prompt.text: A timeout stops a caller from waiting forever when a dependency is

answer.text: A timeout stops a caller from waiting forever when a dependency is slow.

cards.fullLine: A timeout stops a caller from waiting forever when a dependency is slow.

teaching.text: Without timeouts, threads and connections pile up behind one stuck dependency. Set each timeout from the latency budget, and make it shorter than the caller's own patience.

prompt.text: Retries should wait longer after each failure, a pattern called exponential

answer.text: Retries should wait longer after each failure, a pattern called exponential backoff.

cards.fullLine: Retries should wait longer after each failure, a pattern called exponential backoff.

teaching.text: Backoff gives a recovering dependency room. Add jitter, a small random delay, so many clients do not retry at the same instant and create a second spike.

teaching.alt: A failed call retrying after growing, randomised delays until it succeeds

cards.summary: A circuit breaker stops the calls

prompt.text: What does a circuit breaker do after repeated failures?

answer.text: Stops calling the failing dependency for a while.

options: Stops calling the failing dependency for a while
correct: Stops calling the failing dependency for a while

hints: It protects the caller and gives the dependency time to recover.

teaching.text: The breaker opens after a failure threshold, fails fast while open, then allows a probe request after a cool-down. It prevents a slow dependency from consuming every caller thread.

answer.text: The ability to understand internal state from outside signals.

options: The ability to understand internal state from outside signals
correct: The ability to understand internal state from outside signals

hints: You ask new questions without shipping new code.

teaching.text: Monitoring answers known questions. Observability lets you ask new ones from logs, metrics and traces, which is what an incident actually demands.

cards.summary: Logs, metrics and traces are the signals

prompt.text: Logs, metrics and traces are the three main

answer.text: Logs, metrics and traces are the three main signals of observability.

hints: The word used for the data types in OpenTelemetry.
cards.fullLine: Logs, metrics and traces are the three main signals of observability.

teaching.text: A metric says something changed, a trace shows where the time went, and a log explains the detail. Correlating all three is what shortens an incident.

cards.summary: Chaos engineering tests failure on purpose

answer.text: Deliberately injecting failures to test resilience.

options: Deliberately injecting failures to test resilience
correct: Deliberately injecting failures to test resilience

hints: It is a controlled experiment, not an accident.

teaching.text: Start with a hypothesis, inject a bounded failure in a controlled environment, and measure whether the system degrades as intended. Netflix turned this into a discipline.

prompt.text: Graceful degradation keeps the most important features working when part of the system

answer.text: Graceful degradation keeps the most important features working when part of the system fails.

hints: A recommendations panel may disappear; checkout should not.
cards.fullLine: Graceful degradation keeps the most important features working when part of the system fails.

teaching.text: Rank features by importance and decide what turns off first. A page that loads without recommendations is better than a page that never loads.

cards.summary: Health checks separate alive from ready

prompt.text: A liveness check tells the platform whether a process is still

answer.text: A liveness check tells the platform whether a process is still alive.

hints: A readiness check asks a different question.
cards.fullLine: A liveness check tells the platform whether a process is still alive.

teaching.text: Liveness asks whether to restart the process. Readiness asks whether it should receive traffic. Mixing them up restarts healthy pods that are merely warming up.
